articleSummary: Brazil's Federal Police are investigating a theft of high-risk biological material from Unicamp in São Paulo. Initial findings indicate stolen samples include H1N1 and H3N2 influenza A viruses stored in a BSL-3 laboratory. The incident, detected on February 13 during a storage check, led to the arrest of lab coordinator Soledad Palameta Miller, 36, an Argentine national, on charges of theft, fraud, and illicit transport of genetically modified material. All samples have been recovered within the campus; no evidence of outside leakage. Miller is out on bail, with travel ban and restricted campus access during the investigation. Experts warn the theft poses a serious public health risk due to potential spread and severity. Unicamp and CNPEM are Latin America's biotech leaders; Brazil aims to build a BSL-4 facility, reinforcing training and controls.
notes: 高リスク病原体（H1N1/H3N2）のBSL-3施設からの盗難事件。サンプルは既に回収済みで「施設外への漏洩の証拠なし」とされているが、盗難の事実と被疑者逃亡リスク（保釈中）、高リスク病原体の性質から、公衆衛生リスク評価の最優先対象。Argentina（3865483）は発生地域リストに含まれているが、記事サマリーではブラジル（サンパウロ）での事件が主題であり、アルゼンチンは容疑者の国籍情報のみの言及のため、verified_locationsには含めない。

articleSummary: COVID-19 BA.3.2 variant is being monitored by Vietnam's Ministry of Health. The lineage has been detected in at least 23 countries, first identified in South Africa on 22 November 2024. Early data show antigenic changes and potential immune escape in labs, but there is no evidence that BA.3.2 increases severity, hospitalizations, or deaths. WHO and US CDC classify it as a monitored lineage with low public health risk compared with circulating Omicron strains; existing vaccines remain effective against severe disease and death. MOH urges ongoing surveillance, readiness, and rapid detection, with health facilities strengthening risk assessment. Public guidance: do not panic, monitor health, maintain hygiene, and seek care if symptoms appear, especially for the elderly, those with underlying conditions, pregnant women, or other high-risk groups. In Vietnam, 2025 saw hundreds of cases across multiple provinces, with Hanoi, Hai Phong, and Ho Chi Minh City among higher-count locales; no deaths recorded.
notes: BA.3.2はすでに国際的に検出され、WHOが低リスク分類を提示している既知変異株である。ベトナムでの検出は公衆衛生監視の範疇内。重症度増加の証拠がなく、IHR基準2つ以上の該当なし。スクリーニング基準は2つ該当するが、政府の管理可能性が認められているため、フルRRA前段階の経過観察が適切。

articleSummary: Jakarta Selatan, Indonesia—Actress Jessica Iskandar was briefly hospitalized with a high fever suspected to be a bacterial infection after consuming raw foods ahead of a family vacation. Her husband, Vincent Verhaag, said the fever persisted for about seven to eight days, prompting hospital admission where she received IV fluids and antibiotics. By days 10–11 she had improved, and on days 13–14 she departed for a Singapore cruise. Verhaag noted her recovery coincided with the vacation, joking that her only medicine was travel, while he warned against raw foods such as sashimi and urged fully cooked meat. Medical observation attributed the illness to foodborne causes, not GERD; sashimi was cited as a potential trigger two days prior to symptoms. She has since recovered following the trip.

articleSummary: Gianyar Regency, Bali, is preparing to combat dengue fever (DBD), with no tourist-linked cases reported to date. Health data from Gianyar Dinas Kesehatan shows 2023: 1,142 cases and 2 deaths; 2024: 4,476 cases and 5 deaths; 2025: 1,972 cases and 3 deaths. By January 2026, 46 dengue cases had been recorded. On March 29, 2026, officials emphasised village-level prevention, launching simultaneous anti-mosquito campaigns (PSN) since February and community-wide action using 3M Plus: close water storage, regular draining of water containers, recycling potential breeding items, larviciding with powder, keeping larvae-eating fish, using mosquito repellents, and installing mesh screens on vents/windows. Dengue is transmitted by Aedes Aegypti; symptoms range from abrupt high fever up to 40°C, headache, retro-orbital pain, muscle/joint pains, nausea/vomiting, and rash, with a critical phase typically following the fever’s decline after 1–2 days. Tourism-related cases have not been reported.
notes: デング熱はバリ州ギアニャル県の風土病であり、記事は2026年の低い症例数（1月時点で46例）と政府の既知の予防対策（PSN、3M Plus）を記述。観光関連症例は報告されていない。IHR基準には該当しないが、WPROs基準の「長期曝露」「流行しやすさ」に該当し、地域政府の関心が高い点からWATCH判定が適切。

articleSummary: As of March 29, 2026, Ludhiana, Punjab reports an early dengue surge with about 50 patients and hospital reports indicating more than 50 cases, though authorities largely classify most as suspected. The abrupt onset before the usual winter peak has health officials on alert, warning that cases could rise in coming days. Patients exhibit high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, joint and muscle pains, red skin rash, fatigue, dizziness, and vomiting. Reporting from local hospitals is inconsistent, complicating accurate assessment and response. Preventive guidance emphasizes water-source control and personal protection: weekly removal of water from coolers and small containers; cover overhead tanks; use bed nets or repellents at night; empty and dry water storage containers weekly; keep surroundings dry and clean; avoid water accumulation in plastic, coconut shells, and empty tins; spray insecticides around outdoor water sources. Officials urge government-issued dengue treatment guidelines and hospital price transparency to curb arbitrary charges; clothing should cover arms and legs.
notes: 季節外れ（通常は冬期が最大流行時期）でのデング熱発生が重要。確定診断と疑い患者の分類が混在しており、正確な患者数の把握が課題。病院報告の不整合が対応の複雑性を示唆。ウイルス株・遺伝子配列情報は未報告。渡航制限リスクはインドでの国内流行管理能力への懸念が主因。

articleSummary: In the first nearly three months of 2026, Vietnam reported 25,094 hand, foot and mouth disease cases and 4 deaths, more than five times 2025’s 4,900. The southern region accounted for 18,031 cases (71.9%), with 99.3% in children under 10 and 92.7% in the 1–5 age group. Pediatric facilities in the South, including Nhi Dong 1 and Nhi Dong 2, reported rapid increases and numerous severe cases. No antiviral or vaccine exists; management is supportive: antipyretics, analgesics, hydration, nutrition, and oral hygiene; antiseptics on lesions.

articleSummary: Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV), a respiratory virus first identified in 2001, can affect the lungs and airways. Symptoms resemble flu or RSV and thus may be mistaken for a common cold. Transmission occurs via respiratory droplets from coughing or sneezing, through close contact, or by touching contaminated surfaces and then the face. After the regular flu season, HMPV activity rises, typically from late March into April. In most cases, symptoms are mild, but infection can progress to bronchitis or pneumonia, especially in high-risk groups: individuals with weakened immune systems, asthma or other lung diseases, long-term steroid users, and cancer patients. There is no specific antiviral treatment; care is mainly supportive: rest, fluids, and symptom-relief meds as advised. Seek medical evaluation for persistent fever or breathing difficulties. Prevent spread by avoiding crowded places, distancing from the sick, and avoiding touching the face. As of March 29, 2026.

articleSummary: Kissing cats does not transmit Toxoplasma gondii to the human brain. Tempo's fact-check (Jakarta, Indonesia) finds cats are definitive hosts, but human infection occurs mainly through ingestion of infected cat feces, not through kissing or routine contact. Transmission occurs if feces are ingested; infected cats shed for up to two weeks, and the parasite matures 1–5 days after excretion and can persist in the environment for months. Humans are mainly infected via undercooked meat, unwashed produce, or contaminated soil. Most people have mild or no symptoms; pregnancy and immunocompromised individuals are at higher risk. Symptoms, when present, include flu-like aches, fever, and headaches; rare severe symptoms include confusion, seizures, vomiting, or diarrhea. Hygiene measures: wash hands after handling cats, wear gloves when gardening, and clean litter boxes; promptly clean urine, feces, or vomit. articleSummary: As of 2026-03-29, authorities report a February theft of samples from a Biosafety Level 3 laboratory at Unicamp's Institute of Biology in Brazil. Police say the incident poses no public health risk because materials never left the campus. Recovered material was sent to the Ministry of Agriculture, which has not disclosed the pathogens involved. Brazilian media cited by g1 list influenza A subtypes H1N1 and H3N2 among the viruses, along with other pathogens that can affect humans and pigs. The suspect, 36-year-old Soledad Palameta Miller, a researcher in bacteriology, virology and food safety at Unicamp, was detained but released on bail; her husband, Michael Edward Miller, a veterinarian and PhD student at the same university, is also named a suspect. No infections have been confirmed.

A sack full of dead chickens was found on the roadside, and dogs are eating them, increasing the risk of infection.
articleSummary: Avian influenza (bird flu) threat rises in Takhtpur, Chhattisgarh, as of 29 March 2026, after sacks of dead chickens were found dumped along the Takhtpur–Nagoi new bypass. Openly discarded carcasses are being scavenged by dogs, raising concerns that the virus could spread to dogs and other birds and reach residential areas. The incident follows earlier bird flu concerns reported from Bilaspur in the same state. Takhtpur and nearby areas host four to five large poultry farms, and the shock of visible poultry deaths has unsettled the local community and disrupted meat supply. With Navratri season typically boosting chicken demand, poultry trade in the region has already taken a hit due to fears of outbreak. The report highlights ongoing risk and the potential for wider spread through animal vectors, underscoring the need for rapid investigation and containment by authorities.
notes: インドのチャッティースガル州タクトプル地域での鳥インフルエンザ事例。死んだ家禽の不適切な道路脇への投棄、犬による捕食による二次感染リスク、地域の4～5つの大規模養鶏場での感染拡大リスクが指摘されている。ナヴラートリ祭での鶏肉需要増加時期での発生であり、地域の養鶏業に経済的影響が出ている。

articleSummary: Indonesia's Ministry of Health issued Circular HK.02.02/C/1602/2026 to heighten measles awareness and protection for medical personnel as measles cases rise and several areas report a public health emergency (KLB). The circular orders hospitals to reinforce screening/triage, establish isolation spaces, ensure PPE, strengthen infection control, and report suspected cases within 24 hours via the surveillance system. The aim is to curb transmission and protect frontline health workers.

articleSummary: Chikungunya grimly surges in Mato Grosso do Sul (MS), Brazil, in 2026: seven deaths and over 3,000 probable cases across 11 municipalities, making MS the national epicenter in the first three months. MS accounts for about 46% of Brazil’s chikungunya deaths to date; seven fatalities in MS include indigenous communities, with 71.4% of MS deaths among Indigenous people and five deaths in Dourados’ indigenous villages. Infant deaths: two babies aged 1 and 3 months; elderly victims aged 60, 69, 73. The latest death (Mar 28) is an ~80-year-old woman from Jardim (239 km from Campo Grande); Jardim reports 261 probable cases and an incidence of 1,065/100k. Bonito recorded a 72-year-old death. National incidence tops MS at 110.7/100k, with 3,237 probable cases; 56.7% of notifications confirmed (55.6% clinical-epidemiological, 44.4% laboratory). Dourados decreed a 90-day health emergency; R$900,000 allocated for surveillance and vector control.

articleHeadline: El Ministerio de Salud alertó sobre un aumento de casos de fiebre chikungunya
articleSummary: Chikungunya fever in Argentina shows 199 confirmed or probable cases, with 145 autochthonous infections; 54% have travel history to Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, or Cuba. Salta province is the epicenter, reporting 122 confirmed and 55 probable cases—a 97% weekly rise—primarily in Salvador Mazza (107), Aguas Blancas (20), and San Ramón de la Nueva Orán (13). The latest week records the first cases in Jujuy and Catamarca. Most patients have favorable clinical evolution. The National Ministry of Health is coordinating with jurisdictions to block transmission, detect fevers, and diagnose promptly. Surveillance confirms autochthonous cases in Tucumán and travel-associated cases in Buenos Aires Province and City, Córdoba, and San Luis. Transmission is by Aedes aegypti; common symptoms include fever above 38°C and joint pain, with potential muscle pain, headache, nausea, fatigue, and rash. No vaccine or specific antiviral exists; treatment is supportive.

articleSummary: African swine fever (ASF) outbreak linked to a Hanoi slaughterhouse led to criminal indictments on March 25, 2026. The Hanoi Police Economic Department identified an eight-person ring tied to Nguyen Thi Hien’s slaughterhouse in Van Phuc, Nam Phu, Hanoi. They sourced diseased pigs from Phu Tho and Tuyen Quang, transported them to Hanoi, slaughtered them, and sold meat in wholesale and retail markets, including to Cuong Phat Food Co., which supplied meals to several Hanoi schools. Some inspectors allegedly colluded to bypass mandatory checks, allowing diseased or dead pigs to be slaughtered. From early 2026 to March 29, about 3,600 ASF-infected pigs (nearly 300 tonnes) were sold into Hanoi markets. The eight charged include Nguyen Thi Hien; Do Van Thanh; Nguyen Thi Binh; Nguyen Van Thanh (Cuong Phat director); Le Ngoc Anh; Nguyen Phong Nam; Nguyen Thi Phuong Lan; Vu Kim Tuan. Charges: food safety violations; abuse of power; fraud.

articleHeadline: Sự gia tăng bệnh tay chân miệng tại phía Nam năm 2026 , 8 ca tử vong ghi nhận
articleSummary: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) outbreaks in southern Vietnam in the first quarter of 2026 have caused eight deaths (Ho Chi Minh City 4; An Giang 1; Can Tho 1; Dong Nai 1; Dong Thap 1). By week 12, the region recorded 17,078 HFMD cases, 1.9 times higher than 2025, with clusters in Ho Chi Minh City, Dong Nai, Tay Ninh, Can Tho and Dong Thap. Enterovirus 71 (EV71) re-emerged, now accounting for 56% of positive samples and linked to about a threefold higher risk of severe disease. In Ho Chi Minh City, 10,886 HFMD cases (outpatient and inpatient) in 12 weeks; 1,992 hospitalizations, with 69% HCMC residents and 31% from other provinces; 221 severe cases (≥2B), 4 deaths, mainly in Ba Ria-Vung Tau. Dong Nai reports 2,223 cases, 74% under 3 years, several severe cases; one death (23-month-old) from shock and myocarditis. Authorities warn schools as transmission hubs (R0 1.1–5.5) and anticipate peaks May–June and September–December, with IVIG shortages and dengue co-circulation risk.

articleHeadline: Dia D de Vacinação marca início da Campanha Nacional contra a Gripe
articleSummary: On Saturday, 28 March 2026, the Day D influenza vaccination launches Brazil’s national flu campaign in Vitória da Conquista, Bahia. The city distributed 25,840 doses of trivalent vaccine covering H1N1, H3N2 and type B across 12 urban health units and four strategic sites, including Centro Cultural Glauber Rocha, Estação de Transbordo Herzem Gusmão, Shopping Conquista Sul and Boulevard Shopping. Vaccination targets align with Health Ministry priority groups; from Monday, 30 March, campaigns extend to all priority groups through 30 May. Groups include children 6 months to under 6 years (two doses for never-vaccinated with a 30-day interval; one dose if previously vaccinated), pregnant women and puerperae, elderly 60+, and special groups such as health workers, teachers, security/rescue/armed forces, people with comorbidities or permanent disability, truck drivers, and port/public transport workers. Health Secretary Fernanda Maron highlighted vaccination as a preventive measure; the Zé Gotinha mascot drew attention at the events.

articleHeadlineTranslated: SUS begins offering rapid dengue test for early diagnosis of the disease.
articleHeadline: SUS passa a oferecer teste rápido dengue SUS para diagnóstico precoce da doença
articleSummary: Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS) begins offering the rapid dengue NS1 antigen test for early diagnosis in the public health network. Published in the Diário Oficial da União on March 26, the test detects the dengue NS1 protein in the first days of infection, enabling rapid identification compared with antibody-based tests. A small blood sample is placed in a device and yields results in minutes, suitable for use in primary care units, outpatient clinics, and hospitals, at no cost to the patient. Early detection supports timely patient monitoring and medical decisions, reducing risks such as platelet depletion, dehydration, and progression to severe dengue. It also improves public health surveillance of viral circulation to inform prevention strategies. Available to all ages and can be requested by doctors, nurses, or biomedical professionals; rollout depends on service organization and SUS system integration, with emphasis during periods of higher dengue activity.
notes: 本記事はデング熱の検査技術導入に関する医療政策のニュースであり、新規の感染症クラスタ発生、異常な流行、または国際的懸念を報告するものではない。ルーチンの公衆衛生対策強化の一環。

articleSummary: An Indonesian medical intern in Cianjur died from pneumonia-complicated measles. Andito, a University of Indonesia graduate, was interning at RSUD Pagelaran and developed measles symptoms—shortness of breath, fever, and red rashes—receiving care at RSUD Cimacan’s emergency department starting March 25, 2026. Despite maximal treatment, he did not survive. The Health Ministry stated the preliminary investigation found measles with pneumonia as the fatal complication. An epidemiological investigation was initiated by the Cianjur Health Office on March 27, 2026. Contacts were given vitamin A to prevent secondary transmission. articleSummary: As of 30 March 2026, Hanoi Police have indicted a pork supply network linked to African swine fever. Since early 2026, about 3,600 pigs infected have been slaughtered and around 300 tonnes of diseased meat flowed into Hanoi markets and to Cuong Phat Foods Co., which supplied several city schools. The scheme sourced diseased pigs from Phú Thọ and Tuyên Quang and transported them to Hanoi for slaughter at Van Phuc centralized slaughterhouse in Nam Phu, Hanoi. Four veterinary officers allegedly aided bypassing mandatory checks, allowing diseased or dead pigs into slaughter. On 25 March 2026, the police opened a case for violations of food safety regulations, abuse of power, and forgery, charging eight suspects including Nguyễn Thị Hiền (slaughter operator), Đỗ Văn Thanh, Nguyễn Thị Bình, Nguyễn Văn Thành (Cuong Phat Foods CEO), Lê Ngọc Anh, Nguyễn Phong Nam, Nguyễn Thị Phương Lan, and Vũ Kim Tuấn.

Malaysia, site of the 1998 Nipah outbreak, has had no more human Nipah cases, though past transmission tied to pig farms near fruit orchards remains a warning. articleSummary: Late 1998–April 1999 Nipah virus outbreak hit Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia, in two pig-farming villages. articleSummary: On March 27, 2026, PAHO/OPS published a new clinical guideline for the management of severe yellow fever in the Americas, aiming to strengthen health-worker capacity and ensure timely ICU referral. Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne flavivirus; jungle cycles involve Haemagogus and Sabethes, with urban transmission possible via Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The guideline offers evidence-based guidance on suspicion, diagnostic confirmation, initial management, severity classification, and comprehensive patient care, complementing the 2023 clinical management guide as part of the 2024–2025 regional health emergency response, during which the average yellow fever fatality rate reached about 45%. In 2025, 346 confirmed cases and 143 deaths were reported across Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, and Venezuela; in the first seven weeks of 2026, 34 cases and 15 deaths across Bolivia, Colombia, Peru, and Venezuela. Vaccination remains the most effective prevention; one dose confers lifelong immunity, and most deaths in 2025–2026 were among the unvaccinated. PAHO will continue vaccination, surveillance, and health-system strengthening.

articleSummary: As of 30 March 2026, a 52-day-old girl in Henan, China, is in critical condition with botulism after drinking honey-based water prepared by her grandmother to ease cough and strengthen lungs. She was admitted to Henan Children’s Hospital with abdominal distention and severe breathing difficulty, diagnosed as severe botulinum poisoning. The case highlights risk from Clostridium botulinum spores in honey, especially in infants under 1 year with immature gut flora. Botulinum toxin disrupts neural transmission, causing weakness, ptosis, dysphagia, and potentially respiratory failure; mortality is about 20–40%. Treatment requires a specific antitoxin, which may be scarce and must be given promptly. WHO and other health bodies advise against honey for children under 1 year and caution about homemade fermented foods. Prevent measures include thorough cooking (toxin inactivated by boiling 100°C for 10 minutes), strict food safety, and avoiding unknown-origin or vacuum-packed products for infants; seek urgent care if symptoms appear.

articleSummary: Campinas, Brazil: Unicamp is under a police investigation for diversion of at least 24 viral strains from a high-security NB-3/BSL-3 laboratory. The pathogens include dengue, Zika, chikungunya, herpes, and Influenza A variants. The scheme involves professor Soledad Palameta Miller and her husband, PhD student Michael Edward Miller, who reportedly accessed the facility outside normal hours since November 2025. On March 21, Federal Police searches recovered part of the infectious material hidden in a biofreezer at the Food Engineering Faculty where Soledad works. Authorities say she attempted to discard other samples and alter labels to impede the forensic process, resulting in temporary arrest for procedural fraud and crime against public health. Anvisa notes no generalized contamination risk if containers remain sealed and frozen; Soledad Miller was released provisionally, with the motive for maintaining a clandestine virus bank under investigation.
notes: 本件はバイオセキュリティ上の重大インシデントであり、IHR基準2項目以上、WPRO基準3項目以上に該当する。しかし記事サマリーではAnvisaが「容器密閉・冷凍状態であれば一般的な汚染リスクなし」と評価している点が重要。実際の流行拡大の証拠がなく、主に盗難・横領事件としての法的側面が強調されている。WATCHとしたのは、今後の展開（容器破損、意図的な放出、密かな実験など）によってはピックアップに変更される可能性があるため。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue, Zika, and Herpes: at least 24 types of viruses were transported in a theft at Unicamp, says TV.
articleHeadline: Dengue, zika, herpes: ao menos 24 tipos de vírus foram transportados em furto na Unicamp, diz TV
articleSummary: At least 24 virus strains, including Dengue, Zika, and Herpes, were transported between Unicamp laboratories in Campinas, São Paulo, after reportedly being stolen from the NB-3 biosafety Virology and Biotechnology Laboratory. Soledad Palameta Miller, Argentine professor at Unicamp, was arrested by the PF and later released with precautionary conditions restricting lab access and travel abroad. Investigations allege she produced, stored, transported, marketed, and imported or exported genetically modified organisms or derivatives without authorization, in violation of CTNBio rules. The PF also probes her husband, Michael Edward Miller, for possible involvement. The theft is believed to have occurred around February 13, with samples dispersed across laboratories, stored in freezers or discarded in trash; some material was sent to the Ministério da Agricultura for analysis. Crimes under investigation include aggravated theft, procedural fraud, and irregular transport of GMOs; Unicamp is cooperating and has initiated an internal inquiry.
notes: 本事案は自然発生的な感染症アウトブレイクではなく、バイオセーフティレベル3（NB-3）の研究施設からのウイルス株盗難に関する犯罪・管理事案である。ブラジル当局（PF：Polícia Federal）が既に介入し、容疑者の逮捕と調査を進めているため、バイオセキュリティ上の懸念は存在するが、従来の感染症流行シグナルとしてのリスク基準とは異なる性質である。したがってWATCHステータスに分類し、バイオセキュリティ/GMO規制違反の観点から経過を注視する必要がある。

articleHeadlineTranslated: This year, mosquitoes may see an epic-level surge? Public health authorities warn.
articleHeadline: 今年蚊子可能迎来史诗级加强？疾控部门提醒
articleSummary: Dengue fever and chikungunya fever are flagged as key mosquito-borne diseases with increased risk of international importation into China in 2026, due to rising travel and global spread of vectors. Warmer temperatures, higher humidity, and increased rainfall are expanding Aedes aegypti breeding sites and prolonging transmission seasons, raising the potential for local transmission and clustered outbreaks in parts of China, with Guangzhou noting heightened public concern. The press briefing emphasizes that imported cases may seed local spread as overseas epidemics are detected. Preventive guidance includes removing standing water weekly, repairing screens, using mosquito nets, wearing light-colored long sleeves, avoiding outdoor activity at dusk and dawn, applying DEET-containing repellents, and using electric insect repellents. No specific case counts were reported. The analysis reflects ongoing global risk and urging proactive vector control to prevent dengue and other arboviruses.
notes: 本記事は実際の感染症クラスターの報告ではなく、中国疾病管理部門によるデング熱とチクングニア熱の国際的流入リスク評価と予防警告である。具体的な症例数は報告されていない。気候変動と国際旅行パターンの変化を背景とした媒介蚊（ネッタイシマカ）の生息地拡大が懸念されている。進行中の警告活動のため、発生動向を継続監視する価値がある。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Vietnam mobilizes to contain the hand, foot and mouth disease outbreak.
articleHeadline: Le Vietnam se mobilise pour contenir l'épidémie de main-pied-bouche
articleSummary: Hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD) outbreak in southern Vietnam, with Ho Chi Minh City reporting 10,886 HFMD cases in the first 12 weeks of 2026, including 1,992 hospitalizations and 221 severe cases. Eight HFMD deaths in the south: four in Ho Chi Minh City and one each in An Giang, Can Tho, Dong Nai, and Dong Thap. Pediatric Hospital No. 2 has admitted hundreds in Q1, many needing ventilation, dialysis, and ECMO; severe forms can progress within 24 hours with nervous, cardiovascular, and respiratory complications. The city records 332 foci (181 in schools, 151 in the community). Enterovirus 71 accounts for about 24% of samples since late 2025. Children under 36 months (about 80% of severe cases) are most at risk; daycare centers are high-risk. Nationwide HFMD cases exceed 25,000 in under three months, nearly fivefold last year; authorities urge intensified surveillance and rapid containment to prevent health system strain, alongside vigilance for dengue.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Huade Ophthalmology | Don't take seasonal colds lightly; viral infections may trigger viral keratitis.
articleHeadline: 华德眼科｜换季感冒别大意，病毒感染可能引发病毒性角膜炎
articleSummary: Viral keratitis, most often caused by latent herpes simplex virus or varicella-zoster virus, can be activated during spring's immune stress (cold, fatigue, sleep loss) and trigger corneal infection in Beijing, China. After initial dormancy in nerve ganglia, these viruses reactivate and spread along the ocular nerves to the cornea, producing painful red eye, photophobia, tearing, foreign-body sensation, and blurred vision. Early symptoms resemble conjunctivitis and are frequently misattributed to heat or fatigue; improper self-treatment—especially antibiotics or steroid-containing drops—can worsen the infection. Characteristic findings include dendritic-branching or map-like corneal ulcers; unchecked infection damages the corneal stroma, causing scarring and potentially irreversible vision loss. Recurrent attacks are common, and elderly, children, and immunocompromised individuals face higher risk. Management requires prompt antiviral eye drops or ointment, and possibly oral antivirals under medical supervision; stopping treatment is discouraged. Seek ophthalmology care promptly, particularly with eye redness and vision changes.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Why Can't a Rice Cooker’s Keep-Warm Function Exceed Four Hours? Bacteria and Cancer Risk Increase Dramatically.
articleHeadline: 电饭煲保温为什么不能超4小时 细菌与致癌风险大增
articleSummary: Do not keep rice in keep-warm mode beyond four hours, as bacteria and carcinogenic compounds can accumulate. In Sichuan Province, China, clinicians warn that rice held at restaurant-style keep-warm temps (60–70°C) increasingly becomes a breeding ground for pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus and Salmonella, especially when top-layer food cools below 60°C or cross-contamination from utensils or saliva occurs. The WHO defines the food danger zone as 5–60°C, within which pathogens proliferate; at favorable temperatures, bacteria can double roughly every 20 minutes. Illness may include abdominal pain and diarrhea, with possible acute gastroenteritis. More worryingly, long-term keep-warm can promote nitrosamine formation from nitrates in leafy greens, a carcinogen linked to liver, stomach, and esophageal cancers. Practical guidance: finish within four hours or refrigerate promptly to prevent bacterial growth and nitrosamine formation.

articleHeadlineTranslated: ABESTIT Malaria: China Shares Its Expertise to Save Africa
articleHeadline: L'ABESTIT Paludisme: la Chine partage son expertise pour sauver l'Afrique
articleSummary: China’s malaria elimination model is being adapted for Africa, notably Tanzania. China achieved WHO certification of domestic malaria elimination in 2021 after decades of campaigns. Core components include systematic surveillance with rapid case notification, standardized treatment protocols, and vector control using insecticide-treated nets and targeted spraying. In pilot Tanzanian zones, active case finding with household-level interventions markedly reduced local transmission. Adaptations prioritize high-transmission areas and align tools with local resources through co-design with national authorities. Central to the approach is reactive surveillance: the 1-3-7 rule—notify cases within 1 day, investigate within 3 days, implement household-level responses within 7 days (treatment of contacts, spraying, nets distribution). China also promotes local production of rapid tests, antimalarials, and nets to cut stockouts, strengthen supply chains, and create jobs, complemented by joint training and knowledge exchange for health workers. Long-term policy sustainability requires durable funding and local ownership to bridge inequalities between countries.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Kongo Central: a cholera outbreak confirmed at the Mbanza-Ngungu Central Prison - ACP.
articleHeadline: Kongo Central : une épidémie de choléra confirmée à la prison central de Mbanza-Ngungu - ACP
articleSummary: Cholera outbreak confirmed at Mbanza-Ngungu Central Prison, Kongo Central Province, southwestern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Since March 27, 2026, at least 11 inmates have died and 74 cholera cases have been recorded among about 800 detainees. In response, the Justice Ministry and Health Ministry ordered a cholera treatment center inside the prison, with dedicated beds; severe cases are referred to hospitals. Medical teams have been deployed to provide ongoing care and to implement prevention measures, including vaccination per public health protocols. Sanitation, disinfection, and drinking-water quality controls are being intensified to curb transmission. To contain the outbreak, new admissions to the prison have been temporarily suspended. The government reaffirmed commitment to protecting inmates and staff and strengthening preventive and response measures.
